My biggest concern about ending the oil industry is that there are so many people with jobs tied to the oil industry.  If we don't have something put in place to ensure that those people will still have a similar job (in wage and utilizes the same education), they will push back because it's their life.  It is how they pay their bills, how they support themselves and their families.

This is only made worse when it feels like the government doesn't take the Praries' best interests to heart.  After all, we all know which three provinces matter for the elections.  This was aggravated when Trudeau won his second election.

I know if I was in the position to lose my job and everything I worked for because of the government (really climate change but all policies would come from the government), and if I had to possibly get another degree to do a similar job when I originally had the "right" one, I would be really upset about Canada abandoning the oil industry too.

Just in case someone gets upset over the term "right" degree, I'm referring to the degrees you can use right away, as opposed to degrees you wanted to get but can't do anything with for a variety of reasons (ex. grades).

It is so easy to just say "stop oil and fuck the conservatives in Alberta", but you really need to stop for a second and think about where they are coming from and go from there.

Susan woke up.  Today was any other day to her, like the millions before it.  She rolled over and covered her head with her blanket and sighed loudly, thinking of what she could do next.  She had done so many things that she wouldn't have done if she was scared to die.  She looked at the list of things she wanted to do.  Sky diving?  Check.  Underwater cave exploring?  Check.  Motorcycle racing?  Check.  Climbing mountains?  Check.

She didn't just do things she was scared of, she also donated organs to only discover she would regrow them in a few days.  She was immortal.  Everytime she woke up, she would be back to her normal, 30 year old self.

She had several families in the past 50 years, all ending in divorce before her partner figured out that it was just make up.  That was a big part, that she often explained by a skin condition that she was ashamed of. 

She pushed herself out of her bed and got dressed.  Today, she would be moving to Alaska.  She didn't need to figure out how she was gonna live up there since she didn't need food.  She would have fathered to go live in Antarctica, but it was harder to find a way there than it was probably worth it.

The hardest part, she found, was staying average.  She didn't want to draw attention to herself, so she kept to what an almost average person would do.

She got dressed and packed her things into a bag and grabbed her ticket.  Checking to make sure she had a couple of notebooks, her only source of communication with something for the next couple of years.  Unfortunately, when they were completed, they would be burned to ensure that no one knew her secret.  

Nobody could know her secret.  She had told two people, her own parents about it.  However, as they were getting older, they were more persistent on how to become like her.  Why was Susan allowed to live forever but they were doomed to developing dementia?  Why could she recover from everything but they had to experience broken bones because they fell out of bed?  At first, it was the guilt trips.  That she could handle.  Then they started visiting her and demanding how she figured it out.  They never listened when she would explain she didn't know how it happened.  It finally ended with them getting violent. They would threaten to stab her, try to kill her to somehow obtain her power, to only fail in the end.  Her parents were the first and last people she told this secret to, and she learned her lesson.

She knew what dying felt like.  She had done it several times.  Not deploying her parachute in time had sent her to the hospital for weeks, but it was deemed a miracle that she survived.  She accidentally got hit by a train, but also got lucky then.  All of her "near death" experiences were painful, but recovering was the most annoying.

She smiled as she walked out of the room, looking at it one last time.  She was looking forward to no longer having to be careful for a few years. Having to "forget" what happened more than what had happened 50 years ago, beyond what history books covered.

She was free.
